changes: scripts/promote-dist.mjs validates and restores package.json bin targets on staging before evicting the current dist, rejects final symlinks and intermediate-symlink escapes, and preserves the old dist on failure. packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts reports only the compiled runtime version and renders version=unknown on probe failure. The regression suite now uses a portable Windows contract while retaining POSIX execute-bit coverage.
usage: Run npm --prefix packages/main run build, then proof-or-stop --version and proof-or-stop doctor. For regression checks run node packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs and node packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs.
expectedOutcome: A dist rebuild leaves packages/main/dist/cli.js executable on POSIX, proof-or-stop remains runnable, unsafe bin symlink paths cannot chmod files outside staging, and doctor reports the compiled version or version=unknown.
actualTranscript: Focused verification passed: red-global-cli-exec-bit reported staging restoration before old-dist eviction plus GREEN c5/c6 symlink protection; global-core-realpath printed ok; packages/main/dist/cli.js was mode 0755 on this POSIX host.
outcomeDiff: No difference on the tested POSIX host; Windows follows the equivalent npm-shim and shebang contract because POSIX mode bits do not apply there.
limitations: Doctor is read-only and reports remediation without changing the host install. POSIX execute-bit assertions do not apply on Windows; Windows validates the shebang and npm command-shim target, content, cleanup, and pre-eviction safety. POSIX chmod-denial injections are explicitly skipped there while c4/c6 retain failure-order coverage.
pitfalls: Executable-bit restoration must stay before old-dist eviction. Post-promotion chmod can replace a working dist before a staging permission failure is discovered; lexical containment alone can follow intermediate symlinks outside staging.
